Upper-Completion Distributed Acoustic Sensing Enabling Virtual Production and GOR Surveillance in Deepwater Subsea Wells
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Deepwater subsea wells require reliable well-level production surveillance despite limited access for intervention and the commingling of production upstream of the host facility. This study evaluates whether permanent distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) fiber installed entirely along the non-producing upper completion can provide a complementary acoustic pathway for daily oil-rate and gas–oil ratio (GOR) surveillance. Data from three deepwater subsea wells were analyzed using daily frequency-band-energy attributes and Random Forest regression. Pressure, temperature, and choke measurements were used for production-day screening and operational interpretation but were not used as estimator inputs. Model performance was evaluated on blind production days with attribute selection nested within leave-one-out cross-validation. Well A, which provided the longest and most completely sampled calibration record, achieved blind-day R2 values of 0.935 for oil rate and 0.873 for GOR, with RMSE of approximately 208 bopd and 15 scf/bbl, respectively. Performance remained strong when neighboring production days were withheld together. Retrospective review of screened days also identified cases in which allocated production references diverged from matched operating conditions while the DAS estimate remained near the characteristic matched-day level, demonstrating the value of DAS as a separate sensor-domain check. Wells B and C did not provide reliable predictive accuracy; their shorter, narrower, or incompletely sampled calibration records show that successful calibration requires sufficient production variation, repeated sampling across that variation, and adequate retained-day count. Depth-resolved analysis in Well A further showed coherent spatial variation in predictive skill, with oil-rate and GOR high-performing channels overlapping at 1.77 times the spatially correlated null expectation. Restricting estimation to these channels did not improve prediction. The results demonstrate that permanent subsea DAS installed for other monitoring purposes can provide an additional, non-intrusive source of well-level production surveillance, while also offering spatial diagnostics of acoustic sensing response along the upper completion.

nodes.name: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
Spatiotemporal Computer Vision Model for Real-Time Liquid Spill Detection to Mitigate Financial and Environmental Risk in Oil and Gas Facilities
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Uncontrolled liquid spills in upstream and midstream facilities represent a significant threat to safety, operational profitability and environmental compliance. Traditional detection methods often suffer from delayed response times, inability to pinpoint the exact leak source, and high rates of false alarms that lead to operator desensitization. This paper quantifies the operational benefits and demonstrates the environmental sustainability value of a real-time Deep Learning and video analytics framework designed to provide immediate spill detection and precise localization across critical areas including wellheads, separators, and storage tank farms. The study evaluates a computer vision AI model capable of processing thermal and optical camera streams continuously. The model detects liquid presence and contours, tracking the region's size across consecutive frames. If the area is growing, the spill is classified as active and an alert is triggered. This temporal tracking approach eliminates false alarms caused by stationary residues or pre-existing stains. By capturing where the spill is growing and its exact onset time, the system constructs an automated forensic timeline, enabling operators to act with precision. The model was validated on a real-world dataset including diverse appearance conditions (White Hot, Black Cold, and optical RGB liquid presentations), seasonal background changes, and varying camera-to-source distances. Field data demonstrates a median time-to-alert of 34.7 seconds across confirmed events, with high-flow events alerted within seconds and incipient weeps detected within minutes, an alert precision of ~90% in a blind field evaluation against confirmed leak events and a labeled evaluation recall of 86.7%, directly addressing alarm fatigue and increasing operator confidence in alert credibility. The system sends video evidence to the control room so operators can verify the event instantly, eliminating the travel time previously required for manual confirmation. This rapid response directly reduces spilled volume, limits secondary damage, and lowers remediation costs. The system's ability to provide an exact "leak start time" transforms Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting from estimated figures to data-driven metrics, supporting zero-spill targets. The novel contribution of this work is the application of spatiotemporal contour tracking to facility-level liquid spill detection, rather than classifying individual frames. The system tracks the spatial growth of candidate liquid regions across consecutive frames, enabling discrimination between active spills and stationary artifacts that are indistinguishable in any single frame. The approach generalizes across thermal infrared and optical RGB modalities without separate models or site-specific retraining.

nodes.name: Gas Lift Evaluation and Production Forecasting Through a Transfer Learning Dual-Track Machine Learning Framework
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract As reservoirs deplete and natural flow declines, artificial lift becomes necessary to sustain production, and gas lift is one of the most applied methods in unconventional horizontal wells. Injecting high-pressure gas lowers the density of the flowing column and increases drawdown, but the production response is not proportional to the gas injected. It is governed by nonlinear interactions among injection rate, wellbore pressures, geometry, and fluid properties. Beyond an optimum, additional gas reduces production. Machine learning captures such relationships well and predicts oil rate with high accuracy, yet that accuracy is almost always measured within the same wells a model was trained on. A companion study of 11 Eagle Ford wells (Al Raisi et al., 2026) reported R2 as high as 0.960 under a random split but strongly negative values under leave-one-well-out (LOWO) evaluation, because field measurements cluster in a narrow band of conditions and much of the gas lift domain is never observed. This study's framework combines two tracks. Track A applies data-driven models to daily field data from the 11 wells. Track B uses a steady-state multiphase flow simulator to build a physics-consistent synthetic dataset in two complementary designs: a broad dataset of 6,000 nodal-analysis cases sampled by Latin Hypercube Sampling, establishing which operating conditions exist and where gas lift helps, and a controlled sweep of 700 scenarios evaluated at 11 injection rates each, resolving how production responds to injection. Together these required 13,700 simulation cases. A deep learning neural network is then trained through a staged transfer learning procedure that pre-trains on the broad dataset, refines on the sweep dataset, and fine-tunes on field data. The simulations reproduce established gas lift behavior, which is what makes them usable as a training signal. Feasibility rises from 90% to 99% with gas lift, 285 of 295 otherwise non-productive cases are enabled, and the resulting performance curves fall into monotonic, plateau, and post-peak decline classes separated by tubing size, wellhead pressure, and fluid properties. Under LOWO evaluation, staged transfer learning raises the average R2 from 0.149 to 0.414, reduces MAE from 70 to 56 STB/D, and lowers MAPE from 56% to 38%. Neither dataset suffices alone: broad-only pre-training yields 0.146 and sweep-only 0.322, so breadth and structure are both required and the order matters. The gains concentrate on wells the baseline fails, most notably Well 4, which moves from a strongly negative to a positive R2. Applied to a well-level injection scenario, the model ranks lift responsiveness across operating states in the physically expected order, supporting open-loop screening and gas allocation. The study also reports a useful negative result: despite 135 post-peak-decline scenarios in training, predicted curves rise monotonically and do not reproduce over-injection. Expanded coverage and explicit physical constraints are therefore complementary rather than interchangeable.

nodes.name: From Reactive to Proactive: A Physics-Guided Cross-Well Knowledge Coupling Framework for Stuck-Pipe Early Warning
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Stuck pipe is a major risk in complex deep drilling. Conventional early-warning methods rely primarily on real-time parameter trends and historical baselines derived from the target well. Without offset-well knowledge providing prior guidance on the expected normal response envelope, these methods have difficulty distinguishing stuck-pipe precursors from normal response deviations caused by formation changes and progressive bit wear, which can lead to false alarms. Meanwhile, subtle and persistent early deviations may remain undetected. Consequently, alarms are often triggered only after risk signatures become pronounced, making the warning process essentially reactive. This limitation is particularly evident when limited target-well data are available. To address this limitation, this study proposes a formation- and bit-state-informed cross-well knowledge coupling framework for proactive stuck-pipe early warning. A sliding-window regression is first used to extract two parameters characterizing the local Torque–WOB relationship. Formation-dependent commonality, interwell variability, and spatial correlations of the dual features are modeled using a hierarchical Bayesian framework combined with Kriging, thereby providing a normal cross-well prior for an unseen target well. Historical bit-run information is then used to correct the prior according to the current bit-usage state. The corrected cross-well prior is dynamically coupled with target-well historical knowledge through precision weighting. Finally, the joint deviation of the real-time dual features from the expected normal state is quantified using the Mahalanobis distance, and an empirical threshold is used to trigger warnings. The framework was evaluated using leave-one-well-out validation on a database containing 81 wells from three drilling blocks and 29 documented stuck-pipe events. The coverage of normal target-well samples increased from 87.6% for the original cross-well prior to 90.2% after bit-state correction and further to 91.0% after knowledge coupling. Of the 13 events missed by the single-well model, 11 were recovered by the coupled model. The final model detected 27 of the 29 events, achieving a detection rate of 93.1%, a missed-event rate of 6.9%, and a false-alarm frequency of 2.1 alarms per 100 m. For successfully detected events, the mean warning lead distance was 4.6 m. Representative cases showed that warning activation could be traced to persistent migration of the α–β features and abnormal Torque growth under relatively stable WOB conditions. Sensitivity analysis further showed that the selected 20 m sliding window and baseline empirical threshold provided a reasonable balance among detection performance, false-alarm control, and warning lead distance. These results demonstrate that cross-well knowledge provides a stable and updateable external reference for target wells with limited historical data and supports interpretable, proactive stuck-pipe early warning.

nodes.name: Development of a Visual Digital Twin Dashboard for Two-Phase and Three-Phase Flow Regime Classification in Industrial Systems
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate classification of multiphase flow regimes is critical for efficient operation in energy and process industries. While significant progress has been made in two-phase flow classification, extending these techniques to three-phase systems introduces additional complexity due to interactions among phases and variations in flow geometry. In this study, we develop a visual digital-twin-based dashboard for real-time classification and visualization of flow regimes in both two-phase and three-phase flows. Experimental data were generated using the multiphase-flow facility at Hamad Bin Khalifa University, whose principal horizontal test section is approximately 6 m long with a 50.8-mm (2-in.) internal diameter and transparent acrylic sections for video observation. The two-phase water-air dataset contains 65 no-leak experiments spanning liquid superficial velocity from 1.0711 to 3.2134 m/s and gas superficial velocity from 0.6252 to 3.4041 m/s. The three-phase oil-water-air dataset contains 36 experiments spanning water superficial velocity from 1.4059 to 3.1427 m/s and air superficial velocity from 0.063 to 0.320 m/s, including 12 no-leak, 12 single-leak, and 12 dual-leak experiments. Flow dynamics were characterized using high-response dynamic pressure sensors to capture time-series pressure signals representative of multiphase flow behavior. In addition, high-speed imaging (up to 2000 frames per second) was employed to capture the visual characteristics of the flow regimes. Supporting measurements included thermocouples, differential pressure sensors, and electrical process tomography to enhance flow characterization. Visual inspection of the three-phase records reveals bubbly and dispersed structures that are more heterogeneous than those in the two-phase water-air reference data, motivating an analysis workflow that preserves the relationship among sensor signals, video, and operating conditions. These synchronized experimental records are organized as digital threads and streamed to the cloud-hosted digital twin software-as-a-service (SaaS) system. As pressure data arrive, deployed leak-detection models analyze the signals, and the visual twin dashboard presents the associated time series, pipeline video, operating state, and mapped detection or localization outputs for operator review. The MGSB two-phase model achieved a mean held-out detection F1 score of 0.930 +/- 0.082 and an F1 score of 0.783 +/- 0.110 under the prescribed input-corruption test. The MGSB three-phase model achieved an F1 score of 0.984, ROC AUC of 0.9987, false-alarm rate of 0.09%, and mean detection delay of 0.03 +/- 0.01 s on an eleven-experiment dual-orifice evaluation matrix. The novelty of this work lies in integrating experimental multiphase flow measurements with AI-based classification and a visual digital twin interface capable of identifying both two-phase and three-phase flow regimes across multiple geometries in real time. This framework provides a practical decision-support tool for industry applications, including pipeline monitoring, flow assurance, separator performance evaluation, and multiphase transport optimization in oil, gas, and broader process industries. By enabling rapid and reliable flow regime identification using minimal sensor inputs, the proposed system has the potential to significantly improve operational efficiency, reduce uncertainty in multiphase transport, and support next-generation digital oilfield applications.

nodes.name: An End-To-End Multimodal VLM Framework for Automated PPE Annotation and Site-Aware SOP Compliance Monitoring
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Traditional computer vision systems for Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) monitoring are constrained by labour-intensive manual labelling and limited contextual awareness. Conventional models identify isolated objects but lack an understanding of spatial layout, equipment states, and procedural logic. As a result, organizations that rely on these systems often find themselves managing a narrow slice of their actual safety exposure: a helmet is either present or absent, a glove is either detected or not, but the surrounding context, whether that equipment is being used correctly, in the right sequence, under the right conditions, remains invisible to the model. This paper presents a centrally hosted, end-to-end AI framework that automates the lifecycle of safety monitoring using a Multimodal Vision-Language Model (VLM). The framework utilizes a foundation VLM to autonomously generate structured training datasets, eliminating manual annotation bottlenecks that have historically slowed the deployment of computer-vision-based safety tools. These datasets facilitate both the training of lightweight convolutional networks and the site-specific fine-tuning of targeted VLMs, allowing organizations to choose the deployment profile that best matches their hardware and latency constraints. By embedding contextual intelligence and procedural reasoning derived from Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into the model's visual grounding, the framework establishes an adaptive paradigm for AI-driven safety monitoring, shifting the industry closer to its "Goal Zero" safety ambitions, the aspiration that no incident, however minor, should be considered an acceptable cost of operations.

nodes.name: Reproduction of substorm auroral currents in the ionosphere using a machine-learning-based emulator and SuperDARN data assimilation
nodes.venue: Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate
nodes.abstract: Auroral electrojet dynamics during isolated substorms are reproduced using a machine-learning-based emulator with SuperDARN data assimilation. Representing such short-timescale variability is important for improving space-weather prediction relevant to technological systems. Reproducing this variability remains challenging for the SMRAI emulator (Surrogate Model for the REPPU Auroral Ionosphere; Kataoka et al., 2024, https://doi.org/10.1029/2023SW003720), where REPPU is the REProduce Plasma Universe global magnetohydrodynamic simulation. SMRAI is trained on ionospheric outputs from a REPPU MHD simulation and primarily produces smooth and gradual variations in auroral currents during substorms. Therefore, we evaluate the performance of SMRAI with SuperDARN line-of-sight velocity data assimilation (Nakano et al.,2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025SW004488), referred to as the SMRAI–SD framework. Two isolated substorm events on 30 and 31 October 2023 are analyzed to assess the performance of the SMRAI–SD. The SMRAI–SD reproduces auroral current variability in closer agreement with observations than SMRAI, as indicated by improved correspondence with the AL and AU indices. Although reproducing AE indices is not the primary objective, they are used to evaluate the performance of the SMRAI–SD approach and to identify its strengths and limitations through comparison with observations and examination of two-dimensional maps of ionospheric electric potential. SMRAI–SD reproduces abrupt changes in the ionospheric potential that are more pronounced than in the SMRAI. This study therefore evaluates whether such abrupt electrodynamic changes are physically consistent and under what conditions they are reliable. The results demonstrate that SuperDARN data assimilation enhances the ability of the SMRAI model to reproduce ionospheric auroral electrodynamics during substorm and supports its application to space-weather forecasting studies.

nodes.name: Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate
Multimodal expressions of mathematical thinking in play-based contexts: Recognising young children’s mathematical competence beyond numbers
nodes.venue: Set: Research Information for Teachers
nodes.abstract: Early mathematical thinking is often missed when assessment focuses only on numbers and symbols. This article explores how young children express mathematical ideas through multiple modes in play-based contexts, including gesture, drawing, construction, movement, and interaction with materials. Drawing on social semiotics, embodied learning, and play-based pedagogy, this article highlights how children engage in mathematical thinking and communication through pattern, spatial reasoning, symmetry, and problem solving. The analysis emphasises the importance of teacher noticing and intentional responses in recognising and extending these moments. It also foregrounds culturally and linguistically diverse ways of knowing, arguing for a broader, more inclusive understanding of early mathematical competence grounded in everyday activity.

nodes.name: FEATS-G: Orbit and quantum sensor performance simulation for future satellite gravity missions
nodes.venue: GRACE/GRACE-FO Science Team Meeting 2026
nodes.abstract: Satellite gravimetry missions GRACE and GRACE-FO have significantly advanced Earth observation by enabling monthly, high-precision mapping of global mass redistributions. These missions have provided unprecedented insights into the system Earth, such as ice sheet and glacier mass loss, sea level rise, terrestrial water storage changes. However, the classical electrostatic accelerometers suffer from their low-frequency drift and are one of the limiting factors. This drawback can be counterbalanced by an accelerometer based on Cold Atom Interferometry (CAI) because of its high long-term stability.The FEATS-G project advances this frontier through end-to-end simulations to evaluate quantum-based satellite mission concepts. The simulations allow for a comprehensive evaluation of future mission concepts and the exploration of novel scientific applications. They also enable the assessment of quantum-based sensors’ added value in distinguishing between different geophysical signals, while preparing the scientific community for the arrival of this new data type.This contribution focuses on the simulation procedure of observations based on quantum technology. The selected mission scenario will be simulated by the orbit propagation software VENQS. The satellites’ surface is modelled by means of finite elements in order to calculate precise non-gravitational forces induced by solar and Earth radiation and atmospheric drag. The non-gravitational accelerations are considered as disturbance and are measured by the accelerometer. The CAI acceleration measurements are simulated considering various error sources, such as detection noise, contrast loss, wavefront aberration and laser frequency noise. Furthermore, rotational effects and rotation compensation methods using a counter-rotating mirror are included. The simulation procedure and methodology and first results are shown. The artificial orbit data and sensor output will later be used in the gravity field recovery process.We acknowledge the support by the European Union for the project FEATS-G (Call: HORIZON-CL4-2025-02-SPACE-81).

nodes.name: AI-Driven Object Detection for Projectile Localization on Trauma X-rays: An Analytical Study of Diagnostic Accuracy and Forensic Utility
nodes.venue: Indian Journal of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology
nodes.abstract: Background: Trauma radiographs may reveal retained bullets or metallic fragments, and early localization can influence further imaging, surgical planning, safety assessment, and forensic documentation. Methods: This feasibility study used a fully synthetic, computer-generated tabular dataset of 400 case-level records divided into 240 training-design records, 60 validation-design records, and a 100-record held-out test set. The 400 records were not pixel-level radiographs: no DICOM, PNG, or other X-ray images were generated for model training, and no YOLOv9 neural network was trained. Instead, ground-truth labels, confidence scores, simulated detector outputs, a simulated time-constrained radiologist first pass, object-level matches, and processing times were produced by a fixed-seed probabilistic simulation (seed 9173) to demonstrate an evaluation framework. The test set comprised 70 projectile-positive and 30 projectile-negative records. Results: The simulated AI output yielded 65 true positives, 5 false negatives, 3 false positives, and 27 true negatives, corresponding to 92.0% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 90.0% specificity, 95.6% precision, and a 94.2% F1 score; ROC-AUC was 0.972. The simulated radiologist first pass was correct in 83.0% of test records. In paired correctness analysis, AI alone was correct in 12 records and the radiologist alone in 3 (exact McNemar p=0.035). Of 145 synthetic annotated fragments, 136 were matched, with mean IoU 0.828, mAP@0.50=0.937, and mAP@0.50:0.95=0.593. Conclusion: These values are simulation outputs and do not constitute evidence that YOLOv9 detects projectiles on patient radiographs. The study demonstrates a reproducible analysis plan that requires validation on authentic multicentre radiographs, independent annotation, external testing, calibration, human-factors evaluation, and forensic governance before any clinical use.

nodes.name: Indian Journal of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology
YOLO11n-Cucumber: An Efficient Model for Detecting Visual Indicators Associated with Selected Phenological Stages in Greenhouse-Grown Cucumber
nodes.abstract: Automated detection of visual indicator targets associated with selected phenological stages can support image-based monitoring of greenhouse cucumber. However, female flowers and young fruits are often small, partially occluded, and visually similar to adjacent developmental indicators, which complicates their detection in greenhouse scenes. In this study, YOLO11n-Cucumber was developed from YOLO11n for detecting seedling plants, female flowers, young fruits, and marketable fruits. The model incorporates an MDGC-GhostNetV3 backbone for feature extraction, a C2PSA-SCSA module for feature enhancement, and an MSF-CIoU loss for bounding-box regression. Experiments were conducted on a greenhouse cucumber dataset constructed in this study, comprising 3,849 images and 8,791 annotated instances. On the internal test set, YOLO11n-Cucumber achieved a precision of 86.4%, a recall of 84.2%, an mAP@0.5 of 86.8%, and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 61.2%. Compared with YOLO11n, mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by 2.3 and 4.1 percentage points, respectively, while floating-point operations (FLOPs) decreased from 6.4 G to 5.0 G. This reduction in FLOPs was accompanied by increases in the parameter count, from 2.6 M to 3.2 M, and in model size, from 5.6 MB to 6.8 MB. These results indicate that YOLO11n-Cucumber provides an improved accuracy–FLOPs trade-off under the greenhouse image-acquisition conditions of this study. Its generalizability across cultivars, greenhouse types, devices, and environmental conditions requires further evaluation.

nodes.name: Tensor Space and the Causal Limit C: Toward a Dynamic Model of the Universe
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: This revised research collection presents a reconstructed theoretical framework for investigating whether gravity, time progression, light propagation, motion, and causal transmission can be understood as different manifestations of a common underlying structure of cosmic space. The central hypothesis proposes that space is not a structureless vacuum but possesses a fundamental tensor structure characterized by local tensor density (ρT), tensor pressure (PT), and a directional vector (VT). Within this framework, the speed of light C is interpreted as the upper limit of causal transmission, while variations in the proposed spatial structure are examined as possible mechanisms underlying gravitational effects, clock-rate differences, and electromagnetic propagation. The accompanying quantitative verification reports develop candidate mathematical relationships between tensor density, gravitational acceleration, and local clock progression. Calculations are extended from Earth's gravitational field to the solar gravitational field and compared with established relativistic results. Further investigations examine Shapiro time delay and gravitational light deflection, introducing a provisional optical contribution associated with tensor pressure and an effective coupling coefficient calibrated using Cassini observations. A separate series investigates the relationship between time, gravity, and velocity by expressing relativistic time dilation through an effective tensor-density representation. Comparisons include high-speed muons, airborne atomic clocks, optical-clock measurements, and GPS clock corrections. An additional theoretical examination considers whether increasing propagation distance could produce bidirectional redshift between observers with equal local clock rates, using an idealized Earth–Mars thought experiment. This revision also clarifies the relationship between the present framework and earlier studies of cosmic anisotropy, galactic rotation, redshift, and the physical interpretation of time. Previous proposals are retained, reinterpreted, or identified as requiring further examination according to their theoretical and observational status. The results establish a progressively developed phenomenological framework capable of representing several known gravitational and relativistic relationships. However, agreement obtained through equations derived from established physics or coefficients calibrated to existing observations does not constitute independent confirmation of tensor space as a physical entity. The fundamental dynamical equations, independent determination of tensor density and pressure, and distinctive observational predictions remain unresolved. The purpose of this revised collection is therefore to present the current theoretical structure, quantitative achievements, limitations, and criteria for future verification as a coherent foundation for further investigation. Status of Previous Versions Files 00E1–00E5 are retained as historical research materials documenting the earlier stages of this study. They illustrate the development of the original hypotheses and quantitative analyses that preceded the reconstruction of the present theoretical framework. These documents should not be interpreted as fully representing the current theoretical position. Some earlier assumptions have been revised, reinterpreted, or identified as requiring further verification. The current theoretical framework and its quantitative assessments are presented primarily in Files 00A–00D.

nodes.name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Southeast Asian climate and weather extremes simulated by the nextGEMS Earth system models
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Climate
nodes.abstract: This study evaluates nextGEMS Earth system models (ESMs) with storm-resolving spatial scales. Taking advantage of the fine-scale resolution of nextGEMS ESMs, we compare their simulations of Southeast Asian climate and weather systems–strongly influenced by complex sea-land contrasts–to observations and to several CMIP6-class ESMs with coarser horizontal resolution. The nextGEMS ESMs realistically reproduce the sharp structure and seasonal development of the South China Sea cold sea surface temperature (SST) during the winter monsoon season, while most of the selected CMIP6 ESMs fail to simulate these cold SST characteristics. The nextGEMS ESMs also represent the climatological precipitation pattern well. On shorter time scales, they capture the characteristics of monsoon cold surges and Borneo vortices well. Furthermore, dry spells in Southeast Asia are assessed. In particular, nextGEMS ESMs can simulate the increase in winter dry days around the equator during intense El Niño events. Because Southeast Asia is one of the regions most vulnerable to climate change in terms of wet and dry spells, we highlight the potential benefits of kilometer-scale ESMs for producing climate predictions and assessing climate projections in marginal sea areas.

nodes.name: Physics-Guided Neural Phase Demodulation for Non-Contact Laser-Ultrasound Sensing of Corneal Phantom Deformation
nodes.venue: Biosensors
nodes.abstract: Non-contact detection of weak, transient acoustic signals is essential for photoacoustic and laser-ultrasound (LUS) bioimaging, including the assessment of corneal deformation and thickness variation. Passive 3 × 3 fiber-coupler interferometers provide phase-diverse sensing without external modulation; however, conventional ellipse-based calibration becomes unreliable when the measured phase excursion covers only a small fraction of the characteristic ellipse, as in nanometer-scale corneal responses. This study presents a physics-guided temporal convolutional network (PG-TCN) that directly maps two nonideal interferometric outputs to a continuous dynamic phase signal without ellipse fitting or separate phase unwrapping during inference. The model combines dilated one-dimensional convolutions with interferometric-consistency and temporal-regularization losses. Tests using PZT-modulated calibration signals acquired under several static chamber pressures of 10, 15, 20, and 25 kPa showed lower mean absolute error, higher normalized cross-correlation, and lower displacement RMSE than a CNN-LSTM baseline. In corneal-phantom LUS measurements, the first detected echo shifted from 4.632 to 4.488 µs between 10 and 20 kPa, corresponding to a relative thickness reduction of approximately 7.8 µm/kPa. The PG-TCN required 210 ± 18 µs per sequence while using approximately half the trainable parameters of the CNN-LSTM baseline. These results demonstrate a fast physics-guided optical detection framework for non-contact sensing of weak acoustic responses, supporting the use of 3 × 3 optical interferometry as a biosensing approach for LUS and photoacoustic applications.

nodes.name: People as Sensors: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Near-Real-Time Wildfire Detection, Classification, and Geospatial Intelligence from Greek Social Media
nodes.abstract: Citizens' social media posts can provide rapid, complementary situational information during emerging wildfires, alongside conventional sensing and official reporting. For Greek, no annotated wildfire corpus or end-to-end pipeline existed, and most systems stop at binary detection or depend on geotags. We present an end-to-end Greek-language NLP pipeline, a research prototype that turns keyword-retrieved, unlabeled X posts into a geolocated, near-real-time wildfire map: it detects active fires, types them as wildland, urban, or mixed, resolves toponyms, and clusters reports into incidents. On 3,277 manually annotated posts from two fire seasons, to our knowledge the first publicly released, agreement-audited Greek wildfire corpus, fine-tuned transformers reached F2 = 0.911 for detection and macro-F1 = 0.874 for fire type, outperforming classical baselines and, under the tested prompting conditions, two large language models, faster and at zero API cost. On a chronological hold-out of the unseen 2025 season, detection retains F2 = 0.850 (classification recall 0.907); fire-type classification degrades more (macro-F1 0.769 ± 0.085). Spatiotemporal toponym disambiguation raised geocoding accuracy from 54.68% to 80.58% (p < 0.001); a repeatability test revealed gazetteer drift. In a retrospective replay of 12 August 2024 posts, it resolved hundreds of reports of an Attica wildfire into one incident cluster, complementing emergency calls.

nodes.name: PPNet: a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution from UAV orthomosaics
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: Field-scale information on rice seedling distribution is crucial for transplanting quality assessment, site-specific seedling-stage management, and precision agricultural operations. However, seedlings in UAV orthomosaics are small, closely spaced, and easily confused with soil, shallow water, plastic mulch, and shadows, which makes accurate localization challenging. Meanwhile, under high-density planting, existing segmentation-based networks often generate adhesive responses between neighboring seedlings, leading to missed detections and biased counting. To address these issues, this study proposed PPNet, a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution mapping from UAV orthomosaics. The framework uses root-based point annotation and integrates a rice-point perception module (RPPM), an adjacent decoupling module (ADM), and an aggregated attention module (AAM). These modules enhance seedling-point responses, separate adjacent seedlings, and introduce row-structure information. Experiments were conducted on a UAV orthomosaic dataset containing 3,013 image tiles and 220,553 seedling point annotations from different rice-growing regions. PPNet achieved an F1 score of 0.9029, an AP of 0.8881, a counting MAE of 6.99, and an R2 of 0.9553. The method also generated field-scale seedling point maps and density maps under different planting densities and field backgrounds. The results demonstrate that PPNet can provide reliable seedling localization and counting information for crop establishment assessment and targeted seedling management, supporting intelligent agricultural machinery decision-making in precision farming operations.

nodes.name: Neuro-AI: An Integrated Deep Learning Framework for Enhanced MRI-Based Alzheimer’s Disease Classification
nodes.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Capsule Networks
nodes.abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition wherein the early identification of Cognitively Normal (CN), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and AD is of importance to researchers. The different medical equipment used and data collection settings bring about differences that do not pertain biologically when processing the data using automated analysis tools. This research work proposes, Neuro-AI, a deep learning-based pipeline for MRI image preprocessing, harmonization, super-resolution, explainable classification and automatic report generation. T1-weighted MRI images from 202 selected images of OASIS-3 dataset were used in this study and the obtained data are preprocessed by N4 bias correction, skull stripping and intensity normalization techniques. Then a multi-level enhancement process was employed through FusionNet, CycleGAN and SRGAN methods to maximize the imaging variation and spatial resolution from 128 × 128 pixels to 256 × 256 pixels. Then, a pretrained MobileNetV3-Small model was fine-tuned on classifying CN, MCI and AD images. The model achieved an accuracy of 99.95% and a weighted F1-score of 0.9995 on the balanced dataset. The image quality analysis indicated an increase in the average PSNR by 9.60 dB and the average SSIM by 0.0547 with SRGAN processing. GradCAM was used for generating visualization for model predictions, and TinyLLaMA for creating structured reports based on clinical data using Streamlit. While the results indicate the potential of the proposed system, its dependence on the subject level data and lack of multi-site validation prevent any claims about generalization.

nodes.name: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Capsule Networks
Mathematical Anticipation and Representational Coordination Within Van Hiele Levels: Evidence From Pre‐Service Teachers Learning Linear Equations
nodes.venue: School Science and Mathematics
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT This research examines how pre‐service mathematics teachers coordinate algebraic and graphical representations when solving linear‐equation problems. Particular attention is given to mathematical anticipation, including predictions, intermediate results, and verification as participants move between representations. A qualitative interpretive design was used with 126 pre‐service mathematics teachers working in 15 heterogeneous groups. Each group included participants representing the five van Hiele levels of geometric thinking: visualization, analysis, informal deduction, deduction, and rigor. Written and graphical solution artifacts from all groups were examined, and retrospective interviews were used to clarify participants' reasoning. Three representative cases were selected to capture distinctive patterns in the artifacts. The analysis identified three patterns of reasoning: separation of algebraic and graphical representations, emerging but incomplete coordination, and integrated coordination supported by prediction and verification. Across the cases, mathematical anticipation ranged from limited expectations to predictions that guided subsequent actions and were checked against information from other representations. The results indicate that spatial reasoning in linear‐equation problem solving involves more than producing or interpreting graphs. It also involves coordinating representations and using anticipation to guide and evaluate mathematical reasoning. The study provides a process‐oriented account of reasoning within heterogeneous groups organized according to participants' van Hiele levels.

nodes.name: MSMFusion: A Method for Multiscale Dual-Path State Space Modeling for Multimodal Medical Image Fusion
nodes.venue: Biosensors
nodes.abstract: Multimodal medical image fusion aims to integrate information from different imaging techniques to generate a single fused image that is comprehensive and rich in detail. Structural and functional imaging provide high-resolution anatomical details and tissue metabolic information, respectively. Complementary fusion improves quantitative fusion quality and preserves structural and functional information in one view, which aids clinical interpretation. Currently, convolutional neural network-based methods struggle to efficiently capture global features, whereas Transformer-based models excel at global modeling but incur relatively high computational costs. To address the above issues, we propose MSMFusion, a multiscale state-space modeling method for complementary structural–functional medical image fusion. A multiscale feature extraction module first extracts modality-specific multiscale structural features; subsequently, a dual-path MSMamba establishes long-range dependencies with linear complexity: the full-resolution scanning path preserves fine boundaries and textures, while the downsampled scanning path models global context with a more compact sequence; finally, a gated adaptive fusion module estimates spatial–channel weights based on local content to selectively integrate anatomical structure and functional metabolic information. On the Harvard medical image dataset, MSMFusion achieves a mutual information of 2.2181, a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.9390, and a structural similarity of 0.7616 on the MRI–PET task, and also outperforms various representative methods based on CNN, GAN, Transformer, and Mamba on the MRI–CT and MRI–SPECT tasks. Compared with the Transformer backbone, MSMamba reduces the number of parameters from 7.201M to 4.154M and the FLOPs from 476.738G to 159.239G, achieving superior fusion quality at lower computational cost while simultaneously preserving fine anatomical structures and key functional information.

nodes.name: Long-Term Satellite Observations (1998-2025) Reveal Changing Phytoplankton Community Structure and Phenology in the Fram Strait
nodes.abstract: The Fram Strait is the primary gateway between the North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean, where ongoing Atlantification is reshaping hydrographic conditions and marine ecosystems. We applied ML-PhyTAO, a machine learning based retrieval model for Arctic phytoplankton functional types (PFTs), to generate a consistent 28-year (1998–2025) satellite record of total chlorophyll-a (TChla) and major PFT chlorophyll-a concentrations (Chla) in the Fram Strait. Trained with an extensive Arctic phytoplankton pigment dataset and ocean color and environmental products, the model provides robust performance for long-term analyses. Using a dynamic water mass classification based on sea surface temperature and sea ice fraction, the Fram Strait was partitioned into Atlantic Water (AW), Mixed Water (MW), and Polar Water (PW). Distinct seasonal cycles were observed among water masses, with later but more intense phytoplankton blooms in AW. Peak biomass timing advanced by 2–13 days decade⁻¹ for TChla, diatoms, and haptophytes in both AW and MW. Trend analyses revealed declining biomass primarily in MW and the AW–MW transition zone, while haptophytes and dinoflagellates increased within AW. Sea surface salinity, temperature, and sea ice fraction showed stronger and more spatially coherent relationships with PFT variability than modeled nutrient fields, indicating that Atlantification related hydrographic changes are driving shifts in phytoplankton phenology and community composition. This study highlights the unique value of long-term, consistent PFT observations for detecting climate-driven ecosystem change, linking hydrographic variability to community shifts, and supporting future ecosystem and biogeochemical assessments and modelling studies in the rapidly changing Arctic Ocean.

nodes.name: JUICE-JANUS observations of Earth in preparation for the JANUS investigation of Jupiter's atmosphere
nodes.venue: Annales Geophysicae
nodes.abstract: JANUS (Jovis, Amorum ac Natorum Undique Scrutator), the high-resolution camera on the JUICE mission (JUpiter ICy moons Explorer), obtained observations of the Earth during and short-after a Lunar and Earth Gravitational Assist maneuver (LEGA) that was run on 19–20 August 2024. We report on the observations of the Earth that were acquired on 20 August 2024 at a closest approach to the surface of 8408 km, and on 9 September 2024 at a distance of 564 300 km. The close approach observations covered a narrow strip of the Earth, starting in the night-side of the planet and moving over the terminator and day-side. The later observation provided a low spatial resolution portrait of the Earth and the Moon. Here we examine JANUS observations of the Earth as an example of the different science topics that will be addressed in future observations of Jupiter's atmosphere. The Earth night-side images show atmospheric airglow, clouds illuminated by a full Moon, fires in rural areas, lights over the ocean from maritime traffic, city lights, no firm detections of lightning, and two meteor candidates compatible with meteoroids of 1–30 g entering Earth's atmosphere. The day-side images show crepuscular rays under high incidence angles, atmospheric gravity waves on elevated cirrus, sun glint on multi-filter images of the tropical Western Pacific, convective storms, internal waves in the ocean and multiple cloud systems at a variety of spatial resolutions. Some images acquired with the panchromatic filter showed islands such as Luzon and the Big Island of Hawaii. We compare broadband spectroscopic data from JANUS images of the ocean and various cloud systems with spectra from the EnMAP and PRISMA satellites. JANUS images acquired on 9 September 2024 allow to form a multi-spectral view of the Earth at low spatial resolution. The data confirm the expected instrument performance in terms of optical quality and multi-wavelength radiometry precision, and the ensemble of observations contains a wide variety of features that are good analogs to multiple systems in Jupiter's atmosphere.

nodes.name: Integrated Application of Intelligent Sensing and Data Visualization in Violin Instruction
nodes.venue: International Journal of Web-Based Learning and Teaching Technologies
nodes.abstract: The rise of web-based and hybrid learning environments has increased the demand for scalable approaches to monitor violin performance and ensemble coordination. This study proposes a web-based instructional framework that integrates multimodal sensing, multimodal data fusion, three-dimensional visualization, and closed-loop feedback. The framework collects kinematic and physiological signals in authentic teaching scenarios and analyzes relationships between key performance variables, including bow speed and bow pressure, through heatmap-based analysis and distribution modeling. It further constructs a collaboration index, C, to characterize ensemble coordination and provides interpretable feedback for teachers and learners. Across several training cycles, the proposed framework demonstrated improvements in indicators related to accuracy, coordination, and expression, while revealing practical challenges in sensor integration and deployment in actual teaching settings. This study provides a technology-supported model for violin instruction and ensemble learning in web-based and hybrid educational contexts.

Full-Polarization-Sensing MCT Photodetector Enabled by a High-Efficiency Bilayer Plasmonic Metasurface
nodes.venue: Photonics
nodes.abstract: Mercury Cadmium Telluride (MCT) photodetectors operating in the long-wave infrared (LWIR) band play an indispensable role in infrared sensing and imaging. However, conventional MCT detectors respond only to the intensity of incident light and lack the ability to resolve polarization information—polarization being a critical dimension of the electromagnetic field essential for target recognition and scene understanding in complex environments. We overcome this fundamental limitation by monolithically integrating a compact module composed of six individual bilayer metallic metasurfaces onto a planar junction MCT detector, enabling full-state detection of the polarization state of incident light. The metasurface module includes four linear polarization filters with a peak transmission efficiency of 83% and extinction ratios up to 74 dB, as well as two circular polarization filters achieving a transmission efficiency of 94% and an extinction ratio of 36 dB. The circular polarization functionality is realized by tuning the twist angle between the upper cross-shaped metal nanoparticles and the lower trapezoidal structures, thereby breaking spatial symmetry and inducing strong chiral optical responses. The observed ultra-high efficiency arises from the hybridized coupling between localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) supported by the two metal layers. This fully polarimetric MCT photodetector offers both high efficiency and a compact architecture, demonstrating considerable potential for polarimetric infrared imaging, target detection, and quantum information processing.

FPGLNet: A Lightweight Frequency Prior-Gated Network for EEG Emotion Recognition
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Although deep learning-based electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition methods have achieved promising performance, they generally depend on complex network architectures and high computational costs, which limits their deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. Meanwhile, existing approaches mainly focus on local spatiotemporal feature extraction while insufficiently exploiting global frequency-domain dependencies and dynamic information selection during feature propagation, resulting in inadequate spectral information utilization and redundant feature representations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Frequency Prior-Gated Lightweight Network (FPGLNet) for EEG emotion recognition. First, a Mixed Aggregation Convolution (MAC) module is introduced at the input stage to jointly encode EEG spatiotemporal characteristics through temporal and spatial convolutions. Subsequently, a Fused Fourier Convolution Mixer (FFCM) module is developed to model global frequency-domain dependencies through Fourier transform and integrate multi-scale depthwise convolutions for collaborative frequency-spatial feature representation. Furthermore, a Prior-Gated Feed Forward Network (PGFN) is proposed to dynamically generate prior-guided gating weights based on feature responses, enabling adaptive selection and recalibration of discriminative features across different brain regions and temporal segments. This mechanism enhances emotion-related representations while suppressing noise and redundant information. Owing to the lightweight architecture design, FPGLNet achieves an effective balance between feature representation capability, model complexity, and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that FPGLNet achieves classification accuracies of 96.22% and 92.69% on the public SEED-IV and SEED-V datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency prior-gated strategy in improving EEG feature representation while maintaining competitive recognition performance and deployment efficiency.

nodes.name: Environmental Sensing and Borrower Feature Interaction for Uncertainty-Aware Loan Risk Prediction Under Extreme Climatic Conditions
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Extreme climatic events, including severe heatwaves, prolonged droughts, and anomalous flooding, can substantially disrupt agricultural production stability and further increase the risk of agricultural loan default. To address the limitations of conventional credit assessment in fully exploiting environmental sensing information, the scarcity of extreme-disaster samples, and fluctuations in sensing quality, a robust default risk prediction framework integrating agricultural environmental sensing observations, borrower-feature interactions, and uncertainty-aware learning is proposed. First, environmental exposure features and borrower-specific attributes are separately extracted through a dual-branch encoding network, and bidirectional cross-attention is employed to capture nonlinear interactions between climatic conditions and borrower risk. Subsequently, a climate-constrained disaster scenario augmentation mechanism is introduced to expand extreme-environment samples under regional, seasonal, crop-growth-stage, and inter-variable relationship constraints. A stabilized weighting strategy is further constructed by combining stochastic prediction with uncertainty estimation, thereby reducing the influence of highly noisy samples and anomalous observations on model training. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a PR-AUC of 0.791, a ROC-AUC of 0.909, and an F1-score of 0.781 under the combined evaluation of normal and extreme climatic conditions, while attaining a Brier Score of 0.098 and an ECE of 0.027. Under degraded sensing conditions involving missingness, noise, and bias, the model maintains high discriminative capability (PR-AUC of 0.758, ROC-AUC of 0.891, and F1-score of 0.756) and well-calibrated risk estimates (Brier Score of 0.112 and ECE of 0.031). Disaggregated evaluations across perturbation types, sensitivity analyses regarding spatial matching and synthetic labeling, external temporal holdout and cross-regional validations, and post-hoc feature attribution analyses further confirm the robustness and practical interpretability of the framework. Overall, the proposed framework consistently outperforms Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, DNN, LSTM, Deep Ensemble, and the previous model.

nodes.name: Dominant Source Identification in the Propagation of Ocean Observation Uncertainty to Underwater Detection Performance: A Differentiable End-To-End Framework
nodes.abstract: Underwater detection performance is constrained by ocean observation uncertainties that propagate nonlinearly through sound speed profile (SSP) inversion, acoustic transmission-loss (TL) prediction, and sonar performance estimation. We develop a differentiable end-to-end framework that traces observation uncertainty through SSP inversion, acoustic propagation, and passive sonar detection probability (Pd), enabling a quantitative ranking of the dominant uncertainty sources. The framework comprises a Bayesian deep ensemble for SSP inversion, a physics-constrained Fourier neural operator for acoustic propagation, and an analytic sonar-equation module, all implemented in PyTorch with automatic differentiation. Applied to the eddy-active northern South China Sea using the SCSORA reanalysis and validated against independent glider observations, bias-corrected Sobol' first-order indices show that satellite SST observation uncertainty dominates detection-performance uncertainty in deep water (S1 ≈ 0.38–0.52, conditional on the upper-200 m water column), exceeding the acoustic model structural error (S1 ≈ 0.10–0.19). The ranking is robust to a factor-of-two variation in the assigned acoustic structural-error variance and to the choice of attribution scheme (Sobol' vs. Shapley). A paired bootstrap test of a cross-training experiment indicates a small but significant sensitivity of the SST index to the training configuration (ΔS1 = 0.052; 95% CI [0.018, 0.086]), which does not alter the qualitative ranking. In shallow-shelf environments, seabed geoacoustic uncertainty prevails (S1 ≈ 0.41). The framework operates entirely on publicly available data and provides a quantitative basis for prioritizing environmental-observation resources in naval environmental support. Limitations include the absence of independent winter glider observations and the use of a 200-m SSP truncation in deep-water regimes; both are discussed in the paper.

nodes.name: DA-Transformer: Building Damage Assessment Under Complex Changing Conditions Through Multimodal UAV Data
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Accurate damage assessment is critical for reconnaissance and rescue missions. Damage assessment based on unmanned aerial vehicle images is a relevant topic. However, sharing pre- and post-damage knowledge is hindered by the lack of same-viewpoint images in damage assessment for building restoration and reconstruction work. We propose a novel method for generating images based on the same view before and after damage occurs. A point cloud registration method based on serialized matching is presented for spatial transformation with complex damage variations, achieving lower errors and reducing training time. Then, the transformed data are utilized to train a pre-damage differentiable rendering model, generating the undamaged images of buildings from post-damage drone views. Therefore, damage assessment using a large language model (LLM) is conducted by comparing pre- and post-damage images and point clouds. We also construct pre- and post-destruction datasets based on videos. Our method overcomes the limitation of obtaining paired image data from the same perspective, improving the efficiency of evaluation and reducing the difficulty and cost of data collection. We validated the effectiveness of the method through scaling experiments and real explosion scenarios.

nodes.name: Coimbatore Property Valuator: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Offline Market-Intelligence Framework for Property Valuation Real Estate Market and Trend Prediction Model
nodes.venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science, Engineering and Technology
nodes.abstract: Determination of property value is complicated due to factors of locality, property type, area, accessibility, physical characteristics and market conditions. In this paper, a local framework for property valuation in Coimbatore, India is presented, namely, the Coimbatore Property Valuator (CPV). The system includes a data-acquisition and machine-learning module, and an offline evaluation and market-intelligence module. Property listings are automatically harvested from the web, cleaned, standardized, and enhanced with a locality knowledge base, which provides attributes and context on the locality's micro-market, zone, soil, connectivity, and appreciation. XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost are the algorithms used for separate training of Sale and Rent/Lease pipelines. They make predictions using a weighted log-space ensemble with weights of 0.40, 0.35 and 0.25, respectively. The models are based on area, BHK, market statistics, geographic attributes and property-category features. The mobile app also offers an offline valuation engine that uses processed data to compute locality market-rate baselines and uses transparent, rule-based adjustments. It calculates and compares the seller's asking price with a "fair value" range and categorizes the outcome as Great Deal, Fair Market Deal or Overpriced. It also provides locality connectivity and rule-based appreciation projections. The documented project training run gave an ensemble R² of 0.8510 and 0.8567 for Sale and Rent/Lease, respectively. These values are based on the actual run and are not meant to be viewed as absolute market values. CPV fills in the gaps of previous research by integrating local market information, various transaction methods, ensemble prediction, transparent market adjustment, and offline deployment in a unified framework. It illustrates the complementary use of statistical prediction and domain rules in a practical application to property valuation.

Cause-specific mortality and multimodal risk determinants among 5-year ovarian cancer survivors
nodes.venue: BMC Cancer
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Evidence on causes of death beyond five years after ovarian cancer diagnosis remains limited. We characterized post-landmark cause-specific mortality and evaluated clinical, genomic, biochemical, and socioeconomic determinants among five-year survivors. Methods This cohort study used linked UK Biobank data from women who survived at least five years after ovarian cancer diagnosis. Follow-up was anchored at the fifth anniversary of diagnosis, with delayed entry at the later of this landmark and UK Biobank enrollment. Cause-specific cumulative incidence was estimated using the Aalen–Johansen method. Fine–Gray and cause-specific Cox models evaluated mortality from ovarian cancer, cardiovascular disease, second primary malignancies, and other non-cancer causes. Germline homologous recombination repair (HRR) variants were assessed in participants with whole-exome sequencing data. Results The cohort included 920 survivors, of whom 845 had sequencing data. During post-entry follow-up, 322 deaths occurred: 183 from ovarian cancer, 58 from cardiovascular disease, 42 from second primary malignancies, and 39 from other non-cancer causes. At five years after the survivorship landmark, cumulative incidence was 15.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.3–18.1%) for ovarian cancer death and 7.5% (95% CI, 6.0–9.3%) for the combined competing causes. The adjusted risk difference was − 8.1% points (95% CI, − 10.4 to − 5.8), indicating persistent predominance of ovarian cancer mortality. However, differences were attenuated and CIs included zero among survivors aged at least 65 years, those with more than two comorbidities, and those in the highest deprivation tertile. Advanced stage and serous histology were associated mainly with ovarian cancer mortality. Older age, greater deprivation, higher comorbidity burden, adiposity, and current smoking were associated primarily with cardiovascular mortality; more than two comorbidities yielded a subdistribution hazard ratio of 3.32 (95% CI, 1.86–5.92). HRR carriers had higher second-primary-malignancy mortality than non-carriers (subdistribution hazard ratio, 3.74; 95% CI, 1.88–7.42), although this estimate was based on few events. Conclusions Ovarian cancer remained the principal late cause of death among five-year survivors, while competing mortality became increasingly important in older, comorbid, and socioeconomically deprived women.

nodes.name: Automated Spiral-Arm Pitch-Angle Estimation in Galaxy Images Using Deep Learning
nodes.abstract: Abstract Spiral-arm pitch angle is a compact quantitative descriptor of spiral-galaxy structure and is related to galaxy morphology, kinematics, and central mass concentration. Its large-scale use is nevertheless limited by the scarcity of homogeneous numerical labels and by the sensitivity of conventional measurements to deprojection, noise, dust, and arm fragmentation. We present an end-to-end deep-learning pipeline for continuous pitch-angle estimation from galaxy images. A parametric three-dimensional generator produces spiral galaxies with exact pitch-angle labels and controlled variations in arm number, viewing inclination, dust content, and flocculence. Images are processed by automatic disc deprojection followed by spatial-frequency enhancement using unsharp masking, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation, and Fourier-domain filtering. A MobileNetV2 backbone pretrained on ImageNet is then adapted in two stages for regression. On 2,200 synthetic test images spanning pitch angles of 5°-35°, the full pipeline achieved a mean absolute error of 1.01° and a root mean square error of 1.34°. External validation on 65 Sloan Digital Sky Survey galaxies with literature pitch-angle measurements reduced the mean absolute error from 7.07° without the full preprocessing pipeline to 5.83°, while the root mean square error decreased from 10.42° to 7.61°. The results show that geometry-aware preprocessing substantially improves synthetic-to-real transfer, although residual compression of the predicted pitch-angle range indicates that a larger real labelled sample and explicit treatment of bars and non-logarithmic arms remain necessary.

nodes.name: Autoencoder-based non-intrusive model order reduction for anisotropic and multi-physics problems
nodes.venue: Computational Mechanics
nodes.abstract: Abstract We propose a non-intrusive, Autoencoder-based framework for reduced-order modeling in continuum mechanics. Our method integrates three stages: (i) an unsupervised Autoencoder compresses high-dimensional finite element solutions into a compact latent space, (ii) a supervised regression network maps problem parameters to latent codes, and (iii) an end-to-end surrogate reconstructs full-field solutions directly from input parameters. To overcome limitations of existing approaches, we propose two key extensions: a force-augmented variant that jointly predicts displacement fields and reaction forces at Neumann boundaries, and a multi-field architecture that enables coupled field predictions, such as in thermo-mechanical systems. The framework is validated on nonlinear benchmark problems involving heterogeneous composites, anisotropic elasticity with geometric variation, and thermo-mechanical coupling. Across all cases, it achieves accurate reconstructions of high-fidelity solutions while remaining fully non-intrusive. These results highlight the potential of combining deep learning with dimensionality reduction to build efficient and extensible surrogate models.

nodes.name: An Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Spatial Prediction of Soil Salinity Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing and Environmental Data: A Case Study of Cangzhou, Hebei Province, China
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Soil salinity poses a significant challenge to agricultural productivity and sustainable land management in coastal and semi-arid regions. Soil salinity in coastal agricultural regions is controlled by complex interactions among surface conditions, groundwater processes, soil properties, and terrain characteristics. Accurate spatial prediction requires integrating remote sensing observations with environmental information that represents these processes. This study presents a multi-source deep learning framework that integrates Sentinel-2-derived spectral indices with environmental covariates for regional soil salinity spatial prediction under the environmental conditions of the 2024 sampling period. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is employed to quantify the contribution of environmental variables within the prediction framework and improve model interpretability. A convolutional neural network (CNN) incorporating a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention mechanism is developed as a nonlinear feature representation framework for integrating heterogeneous predictors, while the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) is used to optimize model hyperparameters. The proposed framework achieved the highest predictive performance among the benchmark models, with an R2 of 0.785, an RMSE of 0.928, and an MAE of 0.720. Integrating environmental covariates with spectral features further improves the prediction performance, increasing the R2 from 0.701 to 0.785. The results indicate the potential of integrating multi-source environmental information with interpretable deep learning for spatial prediction of near-surface soil salinity under similar coastal agricultural conditions.

nodes.name: Advanced AI-Based Techniques for Empirical Chronological Mapping of Lava Flows Using Multispectral Satellite Imagery: A Case Study of Mount Etna
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Effusive volcanic eruptions pose significant hazards to populated areas, making the accurate dating of lava flows essential for reconstructing eruptive histories and assessing volcanic risk. Traditional dating techniques, such as radiometric, paleomagnetic and lichenometric methods, are highly reliable but require direct sampling, complex analytical procedures, and substantial financial resources. Satellite remote sensing provides a non-invasive and spatially extensive approach that can complement conventional methods in the regional investigation of exposed volcanic surfaces. This study presents a two-stage hybrid classification–regression framework for empirical age estimation and chronological mapping of historical lava surfaces on Mount Etna, spanning the 17th to the 21st centuries. In the first stage, a Random Forest Classifier distinguishes background, pre-1600 lava surfaces, and post-1600 historical lava surfaces, thereby defining the spatial applicability domain of the chronological model. In the second stage, a Random Forest Regressor estimates age only for pixels classified as post-1600 lava by integrating ten Sentinel-2 surface-reflectance bands, elevation derived from the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), and a binary north-flank spatial indicator. On the balanced pixel-level test dataset, the RFR achieved an R2 of 0.549, a Mean Absolute Error of 66.2 years, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 89.0 years. Using the median prediction for each test eruption, the corresponding eruption-level values were R2=0.701, MAE =51.6 years, and RMSE =67.2 years. Prediction errors were larger for the oldest evaluated surfaces, indicating reduced empirical discrimination near the lower boundary of the calibrated chronological domain. This pattern may reflect calibration-boundary effects, sparse chronological coverage, eruption-specific variability, and possible convergence of surface spectral properties. Comparison with an RBF-SVR showed comparable but metric-dependent performance, without establishing the overall superiority of either regression architecture. Permutation analysis indicated that most predictive information within this dataset was associated with the Sentinel-2 spectral component, particularly the Red Edge bands. The proposed method should therefore be interpreted as a complementary fast empirical lava age-estimation and regional screening framework for exposed historical lava surfaces, rather than as a substitute for radiometric, paleomagnetic, or field-based dating.

nodes.name: A HYBRID DETECTION FRAMEWORK FOR SQL INJECTION: REDUCING FALSE POSITIVES THROUGH SIMILARITY-BASED PATTERN MATCHING AND PROACTIVE DEVELOPER INTEGRATION
nodes.venue: Open Journal of Physical Science (ISSN: 2734-2123)
nodes.abstract: SQL injection (SQLi) is a persistent and critical vulnerability in web applications that allows attackers to manipulate databases, access sensitive data, and disrupt services. Existing detection tools face challenges such as high false positive rates, limited effectiveness against obfuscated attacks, and poor integration into development workflows. This study proposes a hybrid SQLi detection framework that integrates similarity-based pattern matching with real-time feedback mechanisms embedded into Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. The framework uses a novel algorithm that parses input queries into Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), employs fuzzy string matching to detect structural similarities with known attack patterns, and applies a predefined threshold mechanism to reduce false positives. Evaluation results indicate a detection accuracy of 97%, a false positive rate of 4%, and high developer usability, with an average Likert score of 4.6 out of 5. Compared to tools like OWASP ZAP and SQLMap, the framework demonstrates superior performance, particularly in handling complex and obfuscated SQLi patterns. Proactive integration into development workflows positions the framework as a solution not only for addressing SQLi vulnerabilities but also for enhancing secure coding practices, minimising costs, and supporting scalable adoption in DevSecOps-driven organisations. The framework sets a foundation for future advancements, including expanding detection capabilities to vulnerabilities like XSS and RCE and incorporating machine learning for adaptive and dynamic pattern analysis.

nodes.name: A GIS-Based Spatial Categorization of Priority Areas for Environmental Quality Improvement in the Cultural Heritage Areas of Surabaya City, Indonesia<i></i>
nodes.venue: Environmental Research, Engineering and Management
nodes.abstract: Conventional development approaches that prioritize economic growth often overlook social and environmental dimensions, resulting in inequality and declining environmental quality, particularly within cultural heritage areas. This study proposes an integrated analytical framework combining Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to classify heritage kampongs based on slum severity and to spatially assess environmental quality in Surabaya City, Indonesia. Spatial overlay analysis using ArcGIS was employed to identify intersections between designated cultural heritage areas and slum settlements, while primary survey data were utilized to evaluate environmental conditions based on established slum indicators. Subsequently, IPA was applied to identify and prioritize the most critical attributes influencing slum severity. The findings revealed that several heritage kampongs exhibited pronounced slum characteristics, with key issues including inadequate drainage systems, poor road infrastructure, and limited living space per capita. By integrating IPA with GIS-based spatial analysis, this study not only reveals patterns of environmental degradation but also pinpoints priority attributes requiring intervention. The resulting classification and spatial visualization provide a robust basis for formulating targeted strategies to improve environmental quality in urban heritage contexts.

nodes.name: Urban pavement condition assessment with hyperspectral remote sensing: a case study of concrete pavements
nodes.venue: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
nodes.abstract: Purpose Concrete pavements are vital to transportation infrastructure, yet their timely condition assessment remains a major challenge because conventional monitoring techniques, such as visual inspection and the Pavement Condition Index (PCI), are often costly, time-consuming, and spatially constrained. This study examines the applicability and reliability of hyperspectral remote sensing as a non-destructive and scalable method for assessing the condition of concrete pavements. Design/methodology/approach A total of 36 field spectrometer data and Airborne Visible and Infrared Imaging Spectrometer–Next Generation imagery were integrated to analyze concrete pavements. Reflectance data from normal and cracked surfaces were compared to identify diagnostic absorption features and quantify spectral indices, including normalized indices, near-infrared (NIR), and shortwave infrared (SWIR) ratios. Findings The analysis revealed distinct absorption bands at approximately 478 nm, 1,060 nm, and 2,207 nm, corresponding to iron oxide, hygroscopic water, and clay minerals, respectively. Compared with normal surfaces, cracked pavements exhibited a 10–15% decrease in overall reflectance and a significant increase in spectral indices. Regression analysis demonstrated a strong field-to-image correlation (R2 = 0.77–0.81), confirming methodological reliability. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to one urban context; validation is required across diverse regions, materials, and traffic conditions. Practical implications The approach provides a robust and cost-effective method for assessing pavement conditions. Combining field spectroscopy with airborne hyperspectral imagery enables the early detection of deterioration and scalable monitoring to support innovative infrastructure management. Originality/value This research presents a novel framework for monitoring concrete pavements in India, demonstrating the potential of hyperspectral remote sensing to enhance large-scale urban road assessments.
